title: Session handoff: ward-cli worker renewal, 2026-11-01 (Ward release and public gates)
description:

Tree clean apart from untracked .claude/worktrees/. Keep every review worktree (DEC-208).

W-6 WCLI-101 and W-7 WCLI-102 are NOT gates. Version ruled A: 0.1.1 (DEC-255).

RULINGS TO KNOW (DEC-255, opum-doc via the leader): publish route for 0.1.1 is the operator sitting on minim4 (build, ad-hoc sign, codesign --verify --strict gate, gh release upload --clobber, regenerate notes and checksum from the signed bytes, verify the DOWNLOAD against the LOCAL signed file); a plain macOS build FAILS strict verify and a codesign -s - --force copy passes (measured, recorded on WCLI-96); macho-cdhash.mjs agrees with codesign -dvvv on both (measured). CI route for a Mac-signed artifact is WCLI-123 (required before any CI-driven release after the flip; does not gate today). WCLI-120 (hosted macos-14 verify, visibility-gated) stays In Progress until observed runs: AC1 at the first private tag or dispatch run, AC2 after the flip. W-9 notes line dropped (#232); the CI check refusing new /Users/ paths in tracked files (WCLI-104) is NOT started and does not gate. WCLI-84 AC4 (real preview alias approved by the operator) is in the sitting: install 0.1.1, keychain re-approval, ward secret set OPUM_APP_VERCEL_CHECK_TOKEN if absent, ward profile approve vercel-preview-read, ward run, ward audit; I gave the leader the exact commands. WCLI-121 Done; WCLI-122 is the follow-up of it (PR #234).

NOT DONE / OWED: Quest records for WCLI-97, 99, 100, 110, 113, 122 after merge (all unticked, not started on the tracker); WCLI-96 AC1 and AC5 (sitting); the second-half hosted-runner observations; stale references I did not edit: CLAUDE.md line 63 (CI on [self-hosted, Linux, ARM64], tier 2: the owning session or operator decides), ADR 0004, the scripts/publish-release.mjs comment.

TRAPS LEARNED THIS SESSION: git push must be alone in its Bash call; the ownership guard refuses any git command whose target is another worktree (agent-*) and any command whose target is built from shell text such as sed -i with ${{ }}: write mutation drivers as scripts under the scratchpad and run them as python3 <file>; implementers run in isolation worktrees whose branches (fix/wcli-97-stdin-residue, fix/wcli-100-prompt-spoof, fix/wcli-122-verify-gate-tests, docs/wcli-110-flip-docs, fix/wcli-99-public-ci-runners) are checked out THERE, so I pushed WCLI-110 as docs/wcli-110-flip-docs-pr and WCLI-99 from the local branch wcli-99-fix1; a subagent report is not authority; run date -u rather than estimating the time; the lore verification and review profiles have about 0 headroom, so new runbooks go in the implementation profile only and placeholders in runbooks must not be angle-bracketed (portability warning); gh pr checks is briefly empty after a push, wait on the head SHA and row count; a hosted runner reuses a freed inode (project-binding T10).

SKILLS: opum-workflow:opum-sdlc, opum-workflow:opum-handoff, opum-workflow:opum-tool-output, lore. Reply to team-lead, never to opum-agent.
implementationNotes:
ADDENDUM 2026-11-01, written after the handoff landed: #233, #234 and #235 are NOT waiting unchanged; all three came back REQUEST_CHANGES from independent Opus units (relays by team-lead, with its own measurements). The fixes are NOT started; the successor starts on them. Findings, condensed.

#233 WCLI-100 at 38ee43c. BLOCKING (team-lead measured): destinationHostForDisplay (terminal-consent.ts near lines 144 and 158) caps the host at 120 chars and keeps the LEFT end, so the registrable suffix is cut off the [y/N] line; normalizeProfile at 5bf5ec8 accepts https://api.stripe.com.<a x40>.<a x40>.<a x40>.evil.example/ (host length 150), so the line would read api.stripe.com.aaaa... and never show evil.example. Fix (display-only, inside DEC-255): do not cap the host on the answer line (ASCII, no spaces, bounded by maxUrlChars), or keep the TAIL behind a leading ...; add a test with a host over 120 chars asserting the answer line contains evil.example. MEDIUM (accepted by ruling): headers are sorted by name so the declaration picks which 8 show and "N more not shown" points nowhere; name where the full set can be read or file a ward profile show follow-up. LOW: blank-rendering code points outside Zs/Cf pass through (U+3164, U+FFA0, U+115F, U+1160, U+2800, U+034F, variation selectors): escape Default_Ignorable_Code_Point plus U+2800 or note the residual; a backslash is not escaped (escaping not injective, cosmetic); a 118-120 char value is truncated although it would fit (budget is maxChars-3 before the length check); the test comment near lines 313-317 claims line bounds true only for short URLs; INFO escapeForDisplay now shows double spaces as \x20 elsewhere, no breakage found.

#234 WCLI-122 at f1396fd (release.yml untouched, measured). BLOCKING: the defaults/shell ban is a TEXT match; a quoted "defaults":, defaults : or ? defaults is the same YAML key and slips past it, so "defaults": {run: {shell: "true {0}"}} at the top level or verify job level neuters codesign with every test green. Fix: reuse parseWorkflow() and assert EXACT key sets: top level {name, on, permissions, jobs}; jobs.verify {name, needs, if, runs-on, timeout-minutes, permissions, steps}; each verify step its exact key set; confirm Bun.YAML yields on as a string key, not boolean true. MEDIUM (closed by the same fix): env: at the top level or on verify is never read; BASH_ENV with a command substitution can define codesign as a no-op. LOW: the pin check reads only steps[*].uses, also check job-level uses: for reusable workflows; step 0 [^\n]* accepts a same-line suffix (optionally pin the full echo line); cutting runbook near line 129 "held back and re-cut" could be read as a re-tag, point it at the tag rule near lines 136-139. The unit asks for the ten mutations run for real plus the quoted "defaults": as an eleventh (predicted green before the fix), results in the PR.

#235 WCLI-110 plus WCLI-113 at 38a57a3. The six limits W-27..W-32 are accurate; blockers are procedure text. BLOCKING: (1) runbook and SECURITY.md and README tell users to check the keychain dialog "names the binary you installed (~/.local/bin/ward)" and stop otherwise, but nobody has measured the dialog (ADR 0001 near line 93 says not measured; line 35 records the ad-hoc identifier as a.out), so the check gives false assurance or stops an honest user: word it around what is known (the dialog appears right after YOU ran ~/.local/bin/ward and names the opum.ward item); the real text is measured at tonight sitting, tighten after. (2) SECURITY.md gives the button route only; DEC-255 (a1) has the operator enable private vulnerability reporting BEFORE the flip with a read-back, but the text must not strand a researcher if the setting is off: add a qualifier or fallback, do NOT invent an email. (3) runbook step 6 "use its marketplace listing" assumes a listing that does not exist publicly: say no public listing exists yet and point to plugin/skills/ward/SKILL.md, or drop the step. MEDIUM: README quick install should run codesign --verify --strict before install and chain with && so a failed shasum stops it; the notes link the runbook at the TAG (blob/REF_NAME/...), which for v0.1.0 is the old private-repo runbook, so point the regenerated notes at main runbook (release.yml is in #232, coordinate) and reword README near lines 35-36; the lines saying the cut 0.1.0 asset fails step 3 until republished must change, since per DEC-255 (a1) v0.1.0 is NOT republished and its notes get a superseded-by-v0.1.1 line. LOW: add the memory reader and core dump (W-13) to the W-28 list; W-31 no notarisation; SECURITY.md near lines 5-6 "not gaps left for later" contradicts ADR 0001 and WCLI-107, say "deliberate bounds of the v0.1 design"; the runbook cites internal tracker ids; step 3 should say where a public user finds the notes (the releases/tag URL). VERSION: the tree says 0.1.0 everywhere; with 0.1.1 shipping the README and runbook URLs, the --version expectation, step 8 snapshot numbers and the rollback text must read 0.1.1 by ship time (can be the bump PR, make it complete including these docs). SECURITY.md does not state W-2 or W-5, which is fine since both land before the flip.

ALSO: team-lead is spawning Opus units for #232 round 2 (5b607c9), #236 (7b80a75) and #237 (ce4f6a6); their verdicts are not recorded here.
